title: The Clear-Night Siren
hook: If the tornado siren ever goes off on a clear night... don't go down to the basement.
lines: In my little town, the tornado siren only sounds for tests. First Wednesday of the month... at noon.
But my grandpa gave me one rule about it.
If that siren ever goes off on a clear night... don't go down to the basement.
Stay upstairs. Lights off. And wait.
Last night, the sky was perfectly clear. Stars everywhere. Not a breath of wind.
At two in the morning... the siren started to wail.
Porch lights snapped on all down the street. My neighbors ran for their cellars in their pajamas, dragging their kids by the hand.
I stayed upstairs, in the dark. Just like Grandpa said.
Ten minutes later, the siren stopped.
Then a calm voice came over the speaker on the pole. All clear. You can come out now.
One by one, the cellar doors swung open... and my neighbors climbed out.
Slow. Stiff. Not talking. Not one of them went back inside.
They just turned, all together... and looked up at my dark window.
They're still standing out there... waiting for me to come down.
